CausalChain: Elevated IL-6 in the tumor microenvironment -> Activation of JAK2/STAT3 signaling in cancer cells -> STAT3-mediated transcriptional upregulation of iron uptake and storage genes -> Increased intracellular iron accumulation -> Enhanced oxidative stress management and activation of EMT-related pathways -> Promotion of cancer stem cell survival and therapy resistance -> Tumor progression and metastasis
Hypothesis: In cancers characterized by high IL-6 production, the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway drives the upregulation of iron metabolism genes, leading to iron accumulation that supports EMT and cancer stem cell maintenance; thus, combined inhibition of IL-6/STAT3 signaling and modulation of iron homeostasis will disrupt this oncogenic feed-forward loop, reducing tumor aggressiveness and improving therapeutic response.
Abstract: The IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis is well documented for its role in promoting tumor growth, epithelial‐mesenchymal transition (EMT), and therapy resistance. Recent evidence also implicates disturbances in cellular iron homeostasis as a contributor to the aggressiveness of certain cancers. In this context, we propose a novel hypothesis that IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling not only sustains autocrine and paracrine oncogenic loops, but also modulates the expression of key iron metabolism regulators, thereby linking iron overload to enhanced ROS adaptation, EMT, and cancer stem cell maintenance. Targeting both this inflammatory axis and aberrant iron uptake may synergistically reduce tumor aggressiveness and overcome resistance in cancers with elevated iron levels.
